newsitem.title: INDIA: India trade deficit seen worsening in fiscal 97/98.
newsitem.headline: India trade deficit seen worsening in fiscal 97/98.

text.p: India's trade deficit is expected to worsen in fiscal 1997/98 (April to March) owing to imports picking up, NatWest Securities said in a research report on Monday.
"We expect the trade deficit in 1996/97 to be lower at $8.18 billion, against the deficit of $8.94 billion in the previous year," NatWest said in a report on the Indian rupee.
"We expect this to worsen in 1997/98 to $10.22 billion."
It said trade deficit narrowed during the first eight months of 1996/97 as growth in imports decelerated more rapidly than that of exports.

Import growth could continue low till the end of 1996/97, it said. "But we are expecting a revival in private consumption demand during the first half of 1997 and, as a result, import demand should pick up during the second quarter of 1997/98."
